Q: How can I convert a UTC datetime to a local datetime using only the standard library? A:

Since Python 3.9 you can use the zoneinfo module.

First let’s get that time with utcnow():

>>> from datetime import datetime
>>> database_time = datetime.utcnow()
>>> database_time
datetime.datetime(2021, 9, 24, 4, 18, 27, 706532)

Then create the time zones:

>>> from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
>>> utc = ZoneInfo('UTC')
>>> localtz = ZoneInfo('localtime')

Then convert. To convert between timezones, the datetime must know what timezone it is in, then we just use astimezone():

>>> utctime = database_time.replace(tzinfo=utc)
>>> localtime = utctime.astimezone(localtz)
>>> localtime
datetime.datetime(2021, 9, 24, 6, 18, 27, 706532, tzinfo=zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(key='localtime'))

For Python 3.6 to 3.8 you need the backports.zoneinfo module:

>>> try:
>>>     from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
>>> except ImportError:
>>>     from backports.zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

The rest is the same.

For versions earlier than that need pytz or dateutil. datutil works similar to zoneinfo:

>>> from dateutil import tz
>>> utc = tz.gettz('UTC')
>>> localtz = tz.tzlocal()

The Conversion:
>>> utctime = now.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
>>> localtime = utctime.astimezone(localtz)
>>> localtime
datetime.datetime(2010, 12, 30, 15, 51, 22, 114668, tzinfo=tzlocal())

pytz has a different interface which is a result of Python's time zone handling not handling ambiguous times:

>>> import pytz
>>> utc = pytz.timezone('UTC')
# There isn’t any local timezone support, you need to know your timezone
>>> localtz = pytz.timezone('Europe/Paris')

>>> utctime = utc.localize(database_time)
>>> localtime = localtz.normalize(utctime.astimezone(localtz))
>>> localtime

Q: SFINAE for template template parameter A:

My reasoning is the following: HasSerialize<ArbitraryClass> can be instantiated with the second template argument being void_T or wrapper<T>::template type, this being more specialized. Therefore, I would have expected HasSerialize<ArbitraryClass> to inherit from std::true_type.

It is not like that,

HasSerialize<ArbitraryClass> uses primary template for default parameter, so is HasSerialize<ArbitraryClass, void_t>. The specialization doesn't has void_T as second parameter (after substitution), so won't be selected.

HasSerialize<T>::value would be false for any type T.

[..] if there is a way to achieve this kind of SFINAE

You cannot check for every types. BTW, you generally want to check for some specific types (possibly template) only, as you don't call the function with every types.

Q: Are curly brackets used in Lua? A:

I know this is old, but I'm learning some Lua right now and was curious about the same thing. Other than tables, no, Lua does not have curly braces in its syntax. Other languages such as C and C++ do use curly braces for creating explicit local scoping which help with organization, lifetime visibility, and more! If you want to achieve the same thing in Lua, you can do the following:

Source: https://www.lua.org/pil/4.2.html

do
  local a2 = 2*a
  local d = sqrt(b^2 - 4*a*c)
  x1 = (-b + d)/a2
  x2 = (-b - d)/a2
end          -- scope of `a2' and `d' ends here
print(x1, x2)

Q: Error when I run SELECT queries to pull data from DB2 and write to SQL Server A:

The error originates from the IBM iSeries ODBC driver during the parameter binding step of cursor.execute(), before any rows are fetched. The driver inspects the DB2 column definition (e.g. G1R CHAR(10)) and rejects your bound parameter if it's longer than that declared size. SQLExecDirectW in the error message confirms it fails at execute time, not at fetch time.

Your parameter r'192.168.64.1\Tag1' is 18 characters. If the DB2 column it binds against is a CHAR or VARCHAR shorter than 18, the driver throws 22001. Most other ODBC drivers silently truncate or coerce; the IBM iSeries driver is strict.

CAST the column to a wider type in the WHERE clause

This keeps parameterized queries (good for type safety) while removing the size constraint:

# Before
'SELECT "G1ST" FROM "DB2"."TABLE1" WHERE "G1R" = ?'

# After
'SELECT "G1ST" FROM "DB2"."TABLE1" WHERE CAST("G1R" AS VARCHAR(100)) = ?'

Apply this to every query that uses = ? on a string column.

Q: Using await outside of an async function A:

I've been looking into Node.js and I've found that you can actually use await outside async . This is called EcmaScript Top Level Modules . Since your file is treated as a module using ES6 Top level modules , it combines the flexibility of ES6 module importing & CommonJS Async importing . Check it out : https://nodejs.org/learn/asynchronous-work/discover-promises-in-nodejs

import {fs} from "fs/promises"

await fs.readFile('',()=>{})
